data.description:
## Description

What: For each cited drift ticket (7225-7708, bf39-4494, e2b6-1059, e8a9-136f), add a regression case under tests/runners/fixtures/regression/ whose oracle is the corrected verdict, and capture the pre-fix behavior as a self-contained fixture snapshot so the case reproduces the historical drift without checking out pre-fix code. Confirm all regression cases are green on current main. Why: sc-6 turns each past reactive fix into a standing guard, which is the epic's core value proposition. Scope IN: four regression fixtures with corrected-verdict oracles, self-contained pre-fix snapshots reproducing each drift, green-on-main confirmation. Scope OUT: the corpus schema/README (draft-1, reused here); the equivalence harness (draft-3, reused here).

## Done Definitions

- tests/runners/fixtures/regression/ contains a self-contained case for each of 7225-7708, bf39-4494, e2b6-1059, and e8a9-136f, each with its oracle set to the corrected verdict ← Satisfies: sc-6
- Each regression case's pre-fix snapshot reproduces the historical drift (red) without checking out pre-fix code, and the same case is green against current behavior on main ← Satisfies: sc-6

## Considerations

- [Boundary] tests/runners/fixtures/regression/** must be in the plugin-boundary allowlist.
- [Self-containment] Snapshots must reproduce drift without checking out pre-fix code, so each case is durable against engine evolution.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a runner-contract maintainer, I want each cited drift ticket captured as a self-contained regression case whose oracle is the corrected verdict, so that historical drifts cannot silently recur.
